Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 6. Home sweet home
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Housewarming party
- Materials: Toy tea set, food pictures, party checklist, COSYmanuals 'some/any', 'countable/uncountable', and 'I'd like' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• organize a gathering and offer drinks/food
• use countable/uncountable nouns with polite offers

Prior learning: Recycles home and furniture vocabulary from Lessons 21–22.

Next lesson: Lesson 24 recycles home vocabulary to talk about moving problems.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

food — things people eat. Example: The food is delicious.
drink — to take liquid into your mouth. Example: I drink tea in the morning.
water — a clear liquid we drink. Example: Please drink some water.
tea — a hot drink made from leaves. Example: She drinks tea every day.
coffee — a hot drink made from beans. Example: I drink coffee in the morning.
welcome — a friendly greeting to a guest. Example: Welcome to our home!
guest — a person you invite. Example: The guests arrive at seven.
party — a social event with food and music. Example: We have a party on Saturday.
house — a building where people live. Example: They live in a big house.
offer — to ask if someone wants something. Example: I offer my guests some tea.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Welcome to our housewarming party! (welcoming guests)
• Would you like some tea? (offering a drink)
• We have food and drink. (describing what is available)
• Help yourself. (inviting guests to take food)
• There are some guests. (describing a party)
• Is there any water? (asking about availability)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'things people eat'?
Which word means 'to take liquid into your mouth'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Polite offer intonation and the /w/ sound in 'welcome'

welcome /ˈwelkəm/ — stress the first syllable
water /ˈwɔːtə/ — stress the first syllable
guest /ɡest/ — one syllable
offer /ˈɒfə/ — stress the first syllable
Listen and repeat:
Welcome to our party! Would you like some tea?

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'some' in positive sentences and offers, and 'any' in negatives and questions.

Form:
Some vs any: some + plural or uncountable noun (positive/offer). any + plural or uncountable noun (negative/question).

Examples:
• I have some bread.
• We haven't got any milk.
• Have you got any apples?
• Would you like some tea?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I have ___ cheese.
We haven't got ___ eggs.
Have you got ___ fruit?
Would you like ___ coffee?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I have some ...
• I haven't got any ...
• Have you got any ...?
• Would you like some ...?
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What food have you got at home?
• What food haven't you got?
• What would you like to drink?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences with 'some' about your kitchen.
• Write three sentences with 'any' about your bag.
Reading: Housewarming party

Welcome to our housewarming party! We have food and drink for our guests. There is some bread, cheese, and fruit. There are some cakes, too. Would you like some tea or coffee? Yes, please. Help yourself to the food. Is there any water? Yes, there is. We are happy to welcome you to our new house.
What food is at the party?
Is there any water?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Welcome to our new house!
B: Thank you. The house is lovely.
A: Would you like some tea?
B: Yes, please. And is there any water?
A: Yes, there is. Help yourself to the food.
B: Thank you. Everything looks delicious.
What does the guest want to drink?
What does the guest think of the food?
Speaking task: Plan a small party. Write a list of food and drink and offer them to your partner.

• Do you like parties?
• What food do you offer guests?
• What do you say when you welcome someone?
• Do you prefer tea or coffee?
• What is a good housewarming gift?
Role-play: You are hosting a housewarming party. Welcome three guests and offer them food and drink.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a short party invitation and a list of food and drink.
Model: Welcome to ... There is ... There are ... Would you like ...?
